cpu.description: CPU limit as a number of cores, e.g. "1" or "0.5". "0" resets it to the plan's total CPU.

ram.description: Memory limit in gigabytes, e.g. "1" or "1.5"; a "G" suffix is appended unless the value already ends in G. "0" resets it to the plan's total RAM. Megabyte values like "512m" are not converted and end up as "512mG".

body_schema.description: JSON body; if it does not decode as JSON the handler falls back to form fields (service_name, image, cpu, ram, network, healthcheck, environment, add_socket, and parallel volume_name/volume_mount/volume_readonly arrays).

service_name.description: New compose service name: starts with a lowercase letter, only lowercase letters and digits, at least 3 characters. Must not already exist.

image.description: Container image reference, e.g. nginx:latest or ghcr.io/owner/app:1.0.

cpu.description: CPU limit as a positive number of cores, e.g. "1" or "0.5".

ram.description: Memory limit as a positive number followed by M or G, e.g. "512M" or "1.5G".

network.description: Name of a network already declared in the account's docker-compose.yml to attach the service to.

healthcheck.description: Optional compose healthcheck block written as a YAML string; rejected with 400 if it does not parse.

environment.description: Environment variables, one per line as KEY=value or key: value; each is stored in .env under the service's prefix and referenced from the compose file.

add_socket.description: Mount the user's podman socket read-only at /var/run/docker.sock inside the container.

volumes.description: Volume mounts. Entries with an empty name or mount are skipped.

name.description: Existing or new named volume (new names: 3-64 lowercase letters, digits or _, starting with a letter), or a relative folder inside the account like ./data.

mount.description: Absolute path inside the container to mount the volume at.

endpoints.description: Edit a compose service's definition. Replaces the whole service definition, so send every setting you want to keep.

body_schema.description: Replaces the whole service definition, not a partial update: volumes, environment, healthcheck and add_socket that are left out are removed (only labels and extra_hosts are carried over). JSON body with the same form-field fallback as POST /api/containers. A running container is restarted afterwards.

service_name.description: Optional; if sent it must equal the <service> path value, since renaming is not supported.

image.description: Container image reference matching ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._/:@-]{0,254}$, or an image with a ${VAR} templated tag such as nginx:${NGINX_VERSION:-latest}.

cpu.description: CPU limit as a positive number of cores, e.g. "1" or "0.5".

ram.description: Memory limit as a positive number followed by M or G, e.g. "512M" or "1.5G".

network.description: Name of a network already declared in the account's docker-compose.yml.

healthcheck.description: Compose healthcheck block as a YAML string; rejected with 400 if it does not parse. Left out means no healthcheck.

environment.description: Environment variables, one per line as KEY=value or key: value. Replaces all of the service's existing variables; left out means none.

add_socket.description: Mount the user's podman socket read-only at /var/run/docker.sock inside the container.

volumes.description: Full list of volume mounts for the service; left out means no volumes.

name.description: Existing or new named volume (new names: 3-64 lowercase letters, digits or _, starting with a letter), or a relative folder inside the account like ./data.

mount.description: Absolute path inside the container to mount the volume at.

foldername.description: Name of the new directory; must not contain a slash. Fails with 409 if it already exists.

path_param.description: Destination directory relative to /var/www/html; empty or omitted means the docroot root.

endpoints.description: Rename a file or directory.

body_schema.description: JSON body. A form post is also accepted, but then the directory key is path_param instead of path.

path.description: Directory relative to /var/www/html that holds the item; empty or omitted means the docroot root.

old_name.description: Current name of the file or directory inside path; it must exist.

new_name.description: New name inside path. Fails with 409 if that name already exists.

endpoints.description: Delete a file or directory (permanently, or move to trash).

filename.description: Name of the file or directory to delete inside path_param. Not checked for emptiness: if omitted, path_param itself is the target.

path_param.description: Directory relative to /var/www/html that holds the item; empty or omitted means the docroot root.

item_type.description: "directory" deletes recursively; any other value deletes a single file. Ignored for symlinks, which are always just unlinked.

mode.description: "trash" moves the item to the trash; any other value, including the default, deletes it permanently.

endpoints.description: Change permissions on one or more files.

body_schema.description: JSON body. A form post is also accepted, with keys path_param, filename (repeated), permissions, folder_permissions and recursive=on.

path.description: Directory relative to /var/www/html that holds the files; empty or omitted means the docroot root.

filenames.description: Names of the files or directories inside path to change. Names that fail are returned in the errored list.

permissions.description: Octal mode such as 644 or 0755. Setuid, setgid and sticky bits are refused.

folder_permissions.description: Octal mode for directories when recursive is set; defaults to permissions when empty.

recursive.description: For a selected directory, apply folder_permissions to it and every folder under it and permissions to the files; symlinks are skipped.

endpoints.description: Copy a file or directory.

item_name.description: Name of the file or directory to copy, inside path_param.

item_type.description: "directory" copies the whole tree; any other value copies a single file.

path_param.description: Directory relative to /var/www/html that holds the item; empty means the docroot root.

destination_path.description: Destination relative to /var/www/html. If it is an existing directory the item is copied into it under the same name; otherwise it is the new path. Defaults to path_param. Fails with 409 if the destination exists.

endpoints.description: Move a file or directory.

item_name.description: Name of the file or directory to move, inside path_param.

path_param.description: Directory relative to /var/www/html that holds the item; empty means the docroot root.

destination_path.description: Destination relative to /var/www/html; empty means the docroot root. If it is an existing directory the item is moved into it under the same name; otherwise it is the new path. Fails with 409 if the destination exists.

endpoints.description: Run a repository action: create (source remote or local, name, remote_url, remote_user, remote_pass, branch, domain, target_dir, deploy_mode automatic|manual|none, actions), pull, deploy, settings, reset_password or delete (repo = repository name). create and reset_password return push_password once.

body_schema.description: Flat JSON object when Content-Type is application/json, otherwise read as form values. In JSON, true is sent on as "1", false and null are dropped, numbers are stringified; arrays and objects are not supported. Which fields apply depends on action.

action.description: What to do. Anything else returns 400 Invalid action.

repo.description: Name of the existing repository to act on; needed for every action except create.

source.description: create only: clone from a remote URL, or create a local repository you push to over HTTPS.

name.description: create only: repository name; must not end in .git or .lock or contain "..". Defaults to the last URL segment for remote, or to the domain for local.

remote_url.description: create with source=remote: http(s)://host/path, git@host:path or ssh://user@host/path URL. Must not start with - or contain "..".

remote_user.description: create or settings: username for an HTTPS remote; ignored for SSH URLs. In settings, sending this key (even empty) updates the credentials, and an empty value clears them.

remote_pass.description: create or settings: password or token for an HTTPS remote. In settings, empty keeps the saved password.

branch.description: create or settings: branch to deploy; must not contain "..", "//" or "/." or end in / or .lock. Local repos default to main. In settings, a remote repo's branch must already be known (pull first).

domain.description: create only: domain the repository belongs to; it must be owned by the account. Its docroot is the default target_dir.

target_dir.description: create or settings: deploy target inside /var/www/html, absolute or relative to it; must not contain "..".

deploy_mode.description: create or settings: automatic deploys on pull/push (create defaults to automatic and deploys a remote repo right away), manual waits for a deploy action, none never deploys.

actions_enabled.description: create or settings: must be true for actions and actions_container to be saved; otherwise deploy actions are cleared.

actions.description: Shell commands to run after each deploy, one per line, inside actions_container.

actions_container.description: Name of one of the account's containers to run the deploy actions in; required when actions is non-empty.

actions_present.description: settings only: must be true for actions_enabled/actions/actions_container to be applied; otherwise the saved deploy actions are left alone.

Site-manager WP-CLI actions for a WordPress site. Reads: site_info, debug_info, update_info. Changes: update_debug, update_site_information, update_now, update_update_preferences.

query_schema.description: Accepted actions: site_info, update_debug, update_site_information, update_now, update_update_preferences, debug_info, update_info. The WP_DEBUG* flags apply to update_debug, the wp_options keys to update_site_information and the WP_AUTO_UPDATE_* keys to update_update_preferences. Read with r.FormValue, so the same keys also work as a form body.

website.description: Site name (domain or domain/subfolder) the action runs for; checked for ownership.

domain.description: Fallback for website, used only when website is empty.

docroot.description: WordPress install path inside the container, such as /var/www/html/example.com; must not contain '..'.

WP_DEBUG.description: update_debug: 'on' sets WP_DEBUG to true, any other value or absence sets it to false.

WP_DEBUG_LOG.description: update_debug: 'on' sets WP_DEBUG_LOG to true, any other value or absence sets it to false.

WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY.description: update_debug: 'on' sets WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY to true, any other value or absence sets it to false.

SCRIPT_DEBUG.description: update_debug: 'on' sets SCRIPT_DEBUG to true, any other value or absence sets it to false.

SAVEQUERIES.description: update_debug: 'on' sets SAVEQUERIES to true, any other value or absence sets it to false.

siteurl.description: update_site_information: new siteurl option, updated only when the key is sent.

home.description: update_site_information: new home option, updated only when the key is sent.

blogname.description: update_site_information: new site title, updated only when the key is sent.

blogdescription.description: update_site_information: new tagline, updated only when the key is sent.

admin_email.description: update_site_information: new admin_email option, updated only when the key is sent.

users_can_register.description: update_site_information: users_can_register option value ('1' enables registration), updated only when the key is sent.

default_ping_status.description: update_site_information: default_ping_status option value ('open' enables pingbacks), updated only when the key is sent.

blog_public.description: update_site_information: blog_public option value ('1' allows search engine indexing), updated only when the key is sent.

Uninstall Drupal: drops the database and user, deletes every file in the docroot, and removes it from Site Manager.
Clone this Drupal site to another domain (or subdirectory). Requires target_domain and source_db; returns a single JSON response.
Update Drupal to the latest version via drush. Streams newline-delimited JSON progress events, ending with {"status":"Update completed!","version":"..."} or an {"error":"..."} line.
Rebuild the Drupal cache via drush cache:rebuild. Returns {"message":"Cache rebuilt successfully."}.

domain_id.description: ID of the user's domain to install on, sent as a JSON string.

admin_email.description: WordPress admin email; empty means admin@<domain>.

wordpress_version.description: WordPress release to install, 'latest' or a version like 6.5.2.

subdirectory.description: Optional subfolder under the domain's docroot; lowercased, spaces removed, parts may only use letters, numbers, dots, dashes and underscores, up to 200 characters.

wp_set.description: Plugins/themes set slug to install; empty uses the global or user set, 'none' skips sets.

requirements.description: "1", "on", "true" or "yes" (case-insensitive) runs bundle install before starting the app; anything else skips it.

git_repo_url.description: Optional https:// repository to fetch into the app folder on every container start. Silently ignored when the git module is not enabled for the user.

port.description: Port the app listens on inside the container, used for the reverse proxy. If omitted, the proxy targets the service without an explicit port.

cpu_limit.description: CPU cores for the container. Values that are not a positive number fall back to 0.5 instead of being rejected.

mem_limit.description: Memory in gigabytes. Values that are not a positive number fall back to 1.0 instead of being rejected.

pids_limit.description: Maximum number of processes. Values that are not a positive integer fall back to 500 instead of being rejected.

endpoints.description: Look at a git repository and return how deploy would run it: runtime, framework, start command, port and image version. Changes nothing.

repo_url.description: Public https:// git repository URL. Private repos and ssh URLs aren't supported.

endpoints.description: Deploy a git repository to a domain in one call: detect the stack, install it as a Node.js, Python, Ruby or Java app with a reverse proxy, then wait until it answers HTTP. Returns 200 when the app answers, 202 when it is installed but not answering yet (poll /api/deploy/status), 422 when the install failed.

repo_url.description: Public https:// git repository URL. Private repos and ssh URLs aren't supported.

domain.description: Domain on this account to serve the app on, like example.com.

subdirectory.description: Serve the app under example.com/<subdirectory> instead of the domain root.

service_name.description: Container name, defaults to one made from the domain. Must not exist yet.

start_cmd.description: Shell command that starts the app after dependencies are installed, overrides detection. No quotes, backslashes, backticks, .. or new lines. It must listen on 0.0.0.0 and port.

port.description: Port the app listens on inside its container, overrides detection (3000 for Node and Ruby, 8000 for Python, 8080 for Java). Required when app_type and start_cmd are both given.

version.description: Runtime image tag: latest or a number like 20 (Node) or 3.12 (Python).

install_dependencies.description: Run npm install, pip install -r requirements.txt, bundle install or mvn install before starting.

cpu_limit.description: CPU cores for the container, default 0.5.

mem_limit.description: Memory in GB for the container, default 1.0. Framework builds often need 2.

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for the app to answer HTTP before returning 202.

endpoints.description: Health of a deployed app: container state, whether it answers HTTP on its port, the status code, and the newest log lines.

site.description: Site the app was deployed to, like example.com or example.com/blog.

lines.description: How many log lines to return.

content.description: Full BIND zone file content; no carriage returns, only $TTL and $ORIGIN directives allowed, and it must pass named-checkzone.

endpoints.description: Add a DNS record.

name.description: Record owner name, e.g. www or @; a name ending in the domain gets a trailing dot added.

ttl.description: Time to live in seconds, as a number or string; defaults to 3600 when empty.

type.description: Record type, case-insensitive; the server's dns_record_types setting limits which are allowed (default A AAAA CAA CNAME MX SRV TLSA TXT). DMARC is saved as a TXT record named _dmarc.

record.description: Record data. Format checks: NS needs a hostname and a subdomain name, HTTPS/SVCB need priority target [params], SSHFP needs algorithm type fingerprint, URI needs priority weight target, DMARC must start with v=DMARC1 and have no quotes.

priority.description: Priority written between the type and the record data, for MX and SRV records.

endpoints.description: Update a DNS record by line number.

content.description: Replacement zone line(s) written in place of rows row_id through end_row_id; record types must be allowed on the server.

end_row_id.description: Last line number (1-based, inclusive) of the record being replaced, for multi-line records; defaults to row_id and must be a JSON number.

serial.description: Zone serial you last read; if given and it differs from the current serial the update is refused with 409.

endpoints.description: Delete a DNS record by line number.

end_row_id.description: Last line number (1-based, inclusive) to delete for a multi-line record; when omitted or not greater than row_id only that one line is removed.
